newsitem.title: USA: N.Iraq Kurds tell U.S. they want to continue truce.
newsitem.headline: N.Iraq Kurds tell U.S. they want to continue truce.

text.p: Leaders of the rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq have told the United States they want to continue a ceasefire in the area despite recent clashes, the State Department said on Thursday.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the department had been in touch with both Massoud Barzani of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Jalal Talabani of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) about this week's incidents.
"Both leaders ... have assured us that they wish to continue to implement the ceasefire established last October," Burns told a news briefing.
"Both parties have expressed concerns to us about some of these incidents. But they say that both are prepared to remain in discussion with each other about ways to resolve them."

The KDP said in a statement on Wednesday night that the PUK launched attacks on its bases on July 15 in Qasre region, near Iraq's border with Iran. It said this meant the end of their U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
Many cease-fires between the two groups have been called and broken since fighting first flared in 1994.
The United States and its allies imposed a no-fly-zone over northern Iraq after defeating Baghdad's forces in the 1991 Gulf War. Kurdish groups have effectively controlled the region since then.
